newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Korona ups share of stocks in balanced fund.
newsitem.headline: Polish Korona ups share of stocks in balanced fund.

text.p: Poland's Korona mutual fund company raised the share of stocks in its balanced fund's portfolio to 50.1 percent in 1996's first half from 44.3 percent at year-end 1995, Korona said on Monday.
The company said in its interim report that the share of bonds in its portfolio shrank to 15.9 percent from 18.4 percent and that T-bills dipped to 30.5 percent from 32.7 percent.
The remaining 2.1 percent of holdings were in other assets.

Korona said the balanced fund made an operating profit of 7.6 million zlotys over the first half and that its assets rose in that time 121 percent to 36.1 million zlotys, with each unit rising 39 percent in value.
Korona also said it made a net profit from operating activity of 7.6 million zlotys over the first half.
It said the largest stakes in its portfolio were Elektrobudowa (6.2 pct), BPH (5.0 pct) and Stomil Olsztyn (4.9 pct).

Korona is a joint venture between Creditanstalt Securities SA, the Polish broking subsidiary of Austria's Creditanstalt-Bankverein, and Polish state-controlled agricultural bank Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ).
Earlier this month it received approval from the Polish Securities Commission to operate an equity and money-market fund.
